name: ARMOR-NODE-SOLAR-HMI
role: Solar touch screen: shows the batteries and the inverters of the installation from ARMOR-SERVER on a 7-inch wall screen
stack: C++17 (host-tested core, LVGL 9 screens drawn by a simulator) and ESP-IDF firmware for the ESP32-P4 that compiles and has never run on a board
deployment_target: Guition JC1060P470C (ESP32-P4 with ESP32-C6, 7-inch 1024 x 600 screen); the firmware compiles and nothing has run on the board
build: cmake -S tests -B build/host && cmake --build build/host && ctest --test-dir build/host
notes: Written and tested on a computer: the reading of the solar devices and totals that ARMOR-SERVER answers, the decisions behind the screen (old data means read-only, the levels of cells, modules and batteries, blinking never above twice a second), the PIN of the screen (a salted, iterated hash, with locks and a short session), the check before an operation on a battery is offered, a simulator of an installation and the screens themselves, drawn on a computer in eight languages. The firmware for the ESP32-P4 (screen, touch, I2C scan, cable network and a board check screen) compiles in GitHub Actions and has never run on a board. It can be set up from the serial console, keeps its settings in flash, signs in and reads the server, takes a signed update and, in an image of its own, joins Wi-Fi through the ESP32-C6: all off by default and none tried on a board. Nothing here sends an order to a battery.
